rv.q: A love story easy to fall in love with … ... this new two-hander of hers is so good — laugh-out-loud funny and tears-to-the-eyes moving … Grounded in cultural specifics but universal in its appeal, Shifters is a mercurial, quick-witted yet poetic examination of love, memories and grief. … The premise may suggest something of almost rom-com...
This, you see, is the skill of Lombe and the entire Shifters team: to wear tender profundity deceptively lightly.

Time-travel love story with thermonuclear charisma … Benedict Lombe’s multilayered romance benefits from the charm of its two leads at the Duke of York in London … Much excitement has preceded the transfer of Benedict Lombe’s nuanced, beautifully affecting love story from the Bush Theatre — only the third play by a black woman yet to have made...

No wonder Idris Elba and Maya Jama backed this superb romcom … Following its sold-out run at the Bush, this bittersweet love story richly deserves its West End transfer and left its audience whooping … The audience wills them on so much that when their attraction finally explodes in a searing kiss, the audience loudly sighs and whoops in...
Shifters is a brilliant addition to this canon, and to a theatreland that’s finding new audiences to love it, argue with it, and bring it to life.
It's funny, grounded in authenticity and blessed with a pair of leads whose charisma pulls you effortlessly into its bittersweet tenderness.
Lombe’s writing, suffused with wit and warmth, is exquisitely poetic at times.

cn.t: Benedict Lombe's time-hopping romance earns near-universal praise for its witty, poetic script that's both laugh-out-loud funny and deeply moving. Critics hail the two-hander as culturally specific yet universal in its emotional resonance.
